drills.title: A type class for addition
hints: Declare a type class `Add` over α : Type, with a single method add : α → α → α.
Check the type of Add.add with all its arguments made explicit.

drills.title: Adding arrays elementwise
hints: Declare an anonymous instance: whenever α has Add, so does Array α.
Its add on x and y is Array.zipWith applied to addition (as an anonymous two-argument function in placeholder shorthand), x and y.
Evaluate Add.add on the array literals containing 1, 2 and 3, 4.
Evaluate the same sum written with +.

drills.title: Exporting the default value
hints: Export `default` from Inhabited so that it can be used unqualified.
Evaluate default at type Nat, then at type Bool.

drills.title: A default instance for multiplication
hints: Declare a type class `HMul` over α : Type u, β : Type v and an output parameter γ : Type w, with a single method hMul : α → β → γ.
Export hMul from HMul.
Declare an anonymous instance of HMul Int Int Int, with hMul being Int.mul, and mark it as a default instance.
Define `xs : List Int` as the list 1, 2, 3.
Check the type of a lambda over y that maps over xs, sending each x to hMul x y.

drills.title: Classical decidability as a fallback instance
hints: Open Classical.
Declare a noncomputable, scoped instance named `propDecidable` with low priority, giving Decidable a for any a : Prop.
Its value is choice applied, without parenthesising the argument, to a match on em a.
In the Or.inl h case, wrap isTrue h into a Nonempty using the anonymous constructor.
In the Or.inr h case, likewise wrap isFalse h.

drills.title: Coercing Bool to Prop
hints: Declare an anonymous instance of Coe from Bool to Prop.
Its coe sends b to the proposition b = true.

drills.title: Coercing decidable propositions to Bool
hints: Declare an anonymous instance, for any p : Prop with a Decidable p instance, of CoeDep Prop p Bool.
Its coe is decide p.

drills.title: Passing addition around by hand
hints: Define `double`, taking s : Add α (α left auto-bound) and x : α, returning an α: s's add field (by dot notation) applied to x and x.
Evaluate double on 10, passing an Add structure built inline whose add field is Nat.add.
Do the same with add set to Nat.mul, then with add set to Int.add.
